title: rollout-ledger: cohort-synced lifecycle manager with session-stitching and rollback-throttle
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add a canonical rollout ledger service that coordinates cohort-synced canaries, session-affine promotions, and a configurable rollback-throttle to reduce cascade failures. Exposes console controls and tracing hooks for manual holdpoints.
description:
Context: We need a single source of truth for staged model promotions that preserves session affinity and avoids mass rollbacks during noisy metric spikes. Current ad-hoc canary controllers duplicate state across replicas and have produced at least two incidents (SUP-8412) where aggressive automatic reverts caused cascading user-visible regressions.

Motivation: centralize lifecycle state, make promotions lease-backed and resumable, and introduce a rollback-throttle that dampens oscillations while still ensuring safety. This PR implements a new "rollout ledger" controller and API surface that: 1) maintains per-cohort promotion state and lease tokens; 2) stitches sessions across shard boundaries so users are consistently routed during deferred cutovers; 3) enforces a configurable rollback-throttle window and exponential backoff for auto-reverts; 4) emits SLI snapshots per cohort for the console and for fast root-cause; 5) adds manual holdpoint and resume endpoints for human-in-the-loop rollouts.

Summary of changes: - core/controller/ledger/controller.go: new controller that manages RolloutLedger records and coordinates promotions across canary lanes - api/rollout_ledger/v1/types.go: ledger resource schema and validation (TTL, leases, cohort annotation) - routing/session_stitcher.go: session-affinity stitching logic used during phased cutovers - policies/rollback_throttle.go: backoff logic and configuration knobs - console/ui/ledger-panel.tsx: basic console integration to surface cohorts, lease owners, and holdpoints - tests/e2e/ledger_flow_test.go: end-to-end smoke and failure-mode tests - docs/rollout-ledger.md: design doc and operational playbook

Commits (high level): - add initial RolloutLedger CRD and controller scaffolding - implement lease/token semantics and leader transfer tests - add session stitching glue and routing tests - implement rollback-throttle and unit tests - wire up console panel and telemetry exports - add e2e failure injection and playbook examples

Files changed (high level): - core/controller/ledger/controller.go +420 - api/rollout_ledger/v1/types.go +98 - routing/session_stitcher.go +230 - policies/rollback_throttle.go +164 - console/ui/ledger-panel.tsx +210 - tests/e2e/ledger_flow_test.go +88 - docs/rollout-ledger.md +54 - build/test fixtures and CI updates (others)

Testing and validation: - unit test coverage for lease transfer, TTL expiry, and backoff corners - e2e scenario that simulates a noisy metric spike and verifies the rollback-throttle prevents immediate cascade - smoke tests that validate session stitching across two router shards - performance bench: lightweight microbench shows <2ms median added path latency on routing hotpath when ledger lookup cache hits - CI: full test matrix passed after two flake fixes

Review notes and discussion thread (condensed): - Diego: "Can we make the lease token short-lived by default and ensure TTLs are configurable per-tenant?" — reply: "Yes, default TTL is 30s; added per-tenant override in types.go and documented in playbook." - Priya: "Session stitching looks good but needs a clear invariant on idempotence when a promotion is retried." — reply: "Added a compact idempotency key and retried promotion path with deterministic state transitions (see controller.go)." - Ethan: "Concern about too many ledger lookups hurting routing; can we cache aggressively?" — reply: "Added an LRU-style in-memory cache with TTLs and a circuit-breaker on cache failures. Benchmarks included." - Diego (approve): "Looks solid, forwarding to SRE for operational runbook verification."

CI and checks: - unit tests: pass - integration tests: pass - e2e ledger_flow: pass - lint: pass - typecheck: pass - policy scan: pass

Merge: Squash-merged into main after minor test rename and CI green run on 2025-11-17.

Post-merge actions: - rollout-ledger feature gate enabled behind runtime flag; ops to do staged deployment across three regions next week - telemetry dashboards created: rollout.ledger.cohort.* and rollout.ledger.rollback_suppressed_count - added playbook under docs with incident run steps

Rollout behavior and safety model: - Lease-backed promotions guarantee a single active promoter per cohort; leader failover handles crashes with deterministic handoff - Rollback-throttle prevents >N automatic reverts within a window (configurable), and uses exponential backoff per-cohort; manual force-revert remains available via console - Session-stitching ensures that users routed mid-rollout see consistent model variants by mapping session cookies to cohort tokens, with a fallback to cookies-only if ledger service is unavailable

Limitations and follow-ups: - Current implementation keeps ledger in memory with a small write-ahead journal; long-term plan is to add a strongly-consistent backing store for cross-region promotion atomicity (ENG-3178) - Need a migration path for older canary controllers; included a compatibility shim but recommend a short co-existence window - More extensive chaos tests (multi-region partition) planned as follow-up (linked in ENG-3125)

Operational notes: - Default config: TTL=30s, rollback_throttle.window=5m, rollback_throttle.max_actions=2 - Suggested canary policy: start at 1% for 5m, then 10% for 15m, then gated promote - Ops checklist included in docs/rollout-ledger.md

Conclusion: This PR centralizes rollout lifecycle state, reduces blast radius from noisy metrics, and provides clear ops controls for manual interventions. It is intentionally conservative (feature-gated) and includes tests and telemetry to validate behavior in production.
